title: The release gate's rust worktree is made under TMPDIR, which a host with a small /tmp cannot hold
body:
`bin/.devbin/cut/gate`'s rust check (`check_rust`, line 112 at 1e423060f) makes its private worktree with `mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/intent-gate-tree.XXXXXX"` and builds the whole workspace into that tree's own `native/rust/target`. That target runs to gigabytes: the stale one dc removed on 2026-11-11 was 2.4G. On kovacs, `/tmp` is a 1.7G tmpfs, so the 3.3.0 cut's kovacs leg could only pass with a stopgap `TMPDIR` line in hv's `~/.config/molt/env.sh`. A host whose `/tmp` is small or memory-backed cannot run the gate as shipped.

The gate should put its tree somewhere sized for a build that host can name. Candidates are under the project (`tmp/`, which is ignored) or a declared config key. It should not depend on each host's `TMPDIR`. When that lands, the kovacs `env.sh` stopgap can go, which is hv's call.

Found on the 3.3.0 cut. Filed, not built, on vc's word (2026-11-11).
